name: Harmonic Prodigy
oracle_text:
Prowess (Whenever you cast a noncreature spell, this creature gets +1/+1 until end of turn.)
If a triggered ability of a Shaman or another Wizard you control triggers, that ability triggers an additional time.
blocked_sentences: If a triggered ability of a Shaman or another Wizard you control triggers, that ability triggers an additional time.

needs.what: a general `double_triggers` static effect (CR 614.1b-style replacement on the triggered ability itself) that, when a triggered ability of a matching permanent triggers, puts an additional instance of that ability on the stack. It must take a `filter` from `static_filter_keys` naming which permanents' triggers it applies to -- here `{"controller": "you", "subtypes": ["Shaman", "Wizard"], "exclude_self": true}` -- so the doubling is scoped by printed creature subtype and excludes the source. Two details have to be pinned deliberately: (a) the effect applies to *any* triggered ability of a matching permanent (enters, dies, attacks, upkeep, activated-ability triggers), not one nominated event, so it has to hook the trigger-queueing path rather than a specific event; (b) each copy is an independent instance whose targets and modes are chosen separately as it is put on the stack, and multiple such effects on the battlefield stack multiplicatively/additively per the controller's ordering of replacement effects. Note the printed subtype scope is asymmetric -- "a Shaman or another Wizard" -- so `exclude_self` may not simply drop the source from the whole filter: a Shaman that is also this card would still be excluded only on the Wizard half. Either the filter surface needs to express two alternative subtype clauses with different self-inclusion, or the engine must special-case that Harmonic Prodigy is itself only a Wizard so blanket `exclude_self` is correct for this printing.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `static_effects` contains exactly one trigger-doubling entry, `double_land_triggers`, and it is wrong on all three axes. It is hard-scoped to landfall-style triggers that fire when a land enters, so it cannot see a Shaman's dies trigger, a Wizard's upkeep trigger, or an attack trigger. It doubles by event type rather than by which permanent owns the ability, so it carries no filter naming the permanents whose triggers are affected -- there is nowhere to hang `subtypes: ["Shaman", "Wizard"]` or `exclude_self`, even though both keys exist in `static_filter_keys` for effects that do take a filter. And it has no self-exclusion concept at all, since a land-trigger doubler has no reason to ask whether the source is the trigger's owner. Nothing in `ops` substitutes either: `reflexive_trigger` and `delayed_trigger` create new one-shot triggers from a resolving effect, and `copy_spell`/`cast_copy` copy objects on the stack from a resolving effect -- none of them is a continuous static that intercepts another permanent's triggered ability as it triggers, and none of them can be an `abilities` entry that sits on the battlefield watching. Authoring this with `double_land_triggers` would ship a card that doubles the wrong triggers from the wrong permanents; authoring it as an unrestricted doubler would drop both the creature-type restriction and the "another", making the card strictly and silently stronger than printed.
